info.title: Lingara API
info.description: Generate vocabulary lists and lesson plans, and hold tutor conversations, in the languages Lingara teaches. Each call is paid for by the client that makes it: an `allowance` client spends its owner's allowance, and a `metered` client is billed for its usage.

post.description: Streams a list of words at the requested level. The stream sends `started` with the list's details, one `item` event per word, then `done`. Until the list is ready it sends keepalive comments only.

200.description: The list, one word per event

post.description: Starts generating a lesson plan and streams its progress. `started` names the plan as soon as it exists, so a dropped connection can reconnect with `GET /v1/lesson-plans/{id}/stream`. The stream ends with `result` or `error`. A plan served from the library arrives as a lone `result`.

get.description: Rejoins the progress stream of a plan that is still generating. A finished plan answers one `result`. A plan still generating with no live stream to join answers one `pending`; poll `GET /v1/lesson-plans/{id}` until it is complete.

200.description: The plan's remaining progress, then the plan

post.description: Sends one message to the tutor and streams the reply as `delta` events, ending with `done`. Nothing is stored: send the recent conversation in `history`, up to 20 entries. `character` and `situation` set the scene. Requires a paid plan.

get.description: Lists each allowance that applies to your account, with how much is used and when it resets.
Returns the events your client can see, a page at a time, oldest first. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to continue.

200.description: A page of events and the cursor to continue from

post.description: Tells Lingara what happened in your game, such as the learner entering a new place. The event is recorded once and answered with `202`. With `generate: true` Lingara also starts a lesson plan, which needs `lesson_plans:write` and is limited and billed like `POST /v1/lesson-plans`: `reaction` names the plan, and `lesson_plan.ready` or `lesson_plan.failed` follows. Describe the world, never a player's name or chat. A `world.practice_completed` event reports how the learner did on items of a lesson plan they own; it never starts a plan, and Lingara sends you `practice.completed` with the same items.

npc.name: Auntie Lin
npc.persona: a street-food vendor who likes to haggle

get.description: Sends each event your client can see as it happens. The stream ends with `done` after 15 minutes, or with `error`; reconnect with the last `id:` in `Last-Event-ID` to continue without a gap.

200.description: Events as they happen, until `done` or `error`

post.summary: Mint a token for a player
post.description: Vouches for one of your players and returns a token your game or page uses for them for 15 minutes. The first token for a `player_ref` creates a learner for that player; later ones reuse it. Ask again when the token expires; it is never refreshed. Needs a `metered` client.

delete.description: Deletes one of your players and everything they made: their plans, their events and their live tokens. Safe to retry: an unknown `player_ref` answers `204` too.

put.summary: Link a player to their Lingara account
put.description: Links one of your players to the Lingara account that just granted your app access. Call it with the delegated token your server received for that account, never with your client's own token. From then on the player's tokens act as the account, as far as the grant allows: ask for `events:read` or you hear nothing about the player after the link. Settled plans move to the account; a plan still being written stays until you call again. Safe to repeat: a repeat answers `existing` and moves what could not move before. Linking costs you nothing.

delete.summary: Unlink a player from their Lingara account
delete.description: Ends a player's link. The player plays as your guest again from the next call. Nothing moves back: what the link carried stays in the learner's account. A player with no live link, or one already unlinked, answers `404 embed_link_not_found`.

post.summary: Send a line to an NPC
post.description: Sends the player's `line` to a character and streams the character's reply as `delta` events, ending with `done`. Give the character its own fluency in `npc.languages`, and choose with `pedagogy` whether it accommodates the learner. Nothing is stored: send the conversation so far in `history`. Send a `checkpoint` with its open `edges` and the `facts` it may reveal, and the stream adds a `transition` event before `done` when the conversation crosses an edge. Each turn is billed to a `metered` client; any other caller gets `403 embed_needs_metered`.

get.description: Pages through your dialogues, newest first. Filter by `name`; pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page.

post.description: Saves a new dialogue graph as a draft, checked against `dialogue.v1` and its graph rules. An account has at most 20 dialogues.

get.description: Returns one dialogue with its draft and active revision, each `null` when absent, and its warnings.

patch.description: Changes a dialogue's name and nothing else.

put.description: Replaces the draft, checked against `dialogue.v1` and its graph rules. Send the `draft_version` you last read, or 0 when there is no draft; a stale one is `409 dialogue_conflict`.

post.description: Makes the draft the active revision, the one a game loads. Send the draft's `draft_version`; a stale one is `409 dialogue_conflict`.

get.description: Answers the `dialogue.v1` document in its canonical bytes: the active revision, or the draft with `revision=draft`; `layout=omit` drops every `x-` member. Send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged revision is `304`.

get.description: Returns this API description as JSON, for the API version the request is answered under: the one named in `Lingara-Version`, or else the current version. No token is needed.
Returns the AsyncAPI document that describes Lingara's events, for the API version the request is answered under: the one named in `Lingara-Version`, or else the current version. No token is needed.

Lists every API version in the order it was minted, with its `state`, when it was minted and, once deprecated, its sunset date. `current` is the newest supported or LTS version, and `development` is the one still growing; each is `null` until such a version exists. No token is needed. Responses may be cached for an hour.

Returns one API version with its full `history`, its `summary` (in English) and its `spec`. The document at `spec.url` is this version's only when requested with the `Lingara-Version` header set to its id. `spec.sha256` is the hash of its frozen document, and is `null` while the version is still in development. An unknown id answers `404`. No token is needed. Responses may be cached for an hour.

oauth2.description: An OAuth 2.0 access token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A server acting as itself exchanges its client's id and secret at the token URL (`client_credentials`). An app acting for a Lingara user who consents uses the authorization code (`authorization_code`) and then refreshes. A token lasts one hour. Each operation needs one scope.

LingaraVersion.name: Lingara-Version
LingaraVersion.description: The API version to answer this request under. Without it, an access token gets the version its client is pinned to, and a request with no token gets the current version. The version still in development is reached only by naming it here. An unknown version answers `400` with code `api_version_unknown`. `GET /v1/versions` lists the versions.

EventCursor.name: cursor
EventCursor.description: Where to continue from: an earlier page's `next_cursor`, or a stream event's `id:`. A cursor older than 30 days answers `410` with code `cursor_expired`.

EventStart.name: start
EventStart.description: Where to begin without a cursor: `latest` for events from now on, or `oldest` for every event still kept.

EventTypes.name: types
EventTypes.description: Only these event types, comma-separated. Without it, every type your token's scopes can read.

EventLimit.name: limit
EventLimit.description: The most events one page returns, from 1 to 100.

LastEventId.name: Last-Event-ID
LastEventId.description: The `id:` of the last event you received. It takes precedence over `cursor` and `start`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A value you choose for each event and reuse when you retry it: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, such as a UUID. A retry with the same key gets the first answer back and is not billed again, even if its body differs. Without a valid key the request answers `400` with code `idempotency_key_required`.

PlayerRef.name: player_ref
PlayerRef.description: The `player_ref` you minted the player's tokens with, percent-encoded: `guild/42` is `guild%2F42`.

LingaraVersion.description: The API version this response was answered under. Absent until the first version is frozen.

Deprecation.description: When this response's API version was deprecated, as `@` followed by Unix seconds. Present only on a deprecated version.

Sunset.description: The date from which this response's API version may be discontinued. Present only on a deprecated version.

Link.description: A link, with relation `deprecation`, to this API version's details. Present only on a deprecated version.

ApiAllowanceLimit.description: The account's daily API allowance, in credits. Present only on a response to an allowance client's client-credentials token from a spending scope; absent on an unlimited allowance or a call that spends no credits.

ApiAllowanceRemaining.description: Credits left in the account's daily API allowance after this call. Present only on a response to an allowance client's client-credentials token from a spending scope; absent on an unlimited allowance or a call that spends no credits.

ApiAllowanceReset.description: When the daily API allowance resets: the next UTC midnight, in Unix seconds. Present only on a response to an allowance client's client-credentials token from a spending scope; absent on an unlimited allowance or a call that spends no credits.

Error.description: The request was refused. `code` says why, and `error` says it in words.

PaymentRequired.description: A metered client's call was refused before it spent anything. `spend_cap_reached`: the client or its account has reached its monthly spending limit; raise the limit on the Integrations page. `metered_billing_inactive`: usage billing is not active for this account; set it up, or update the payment method, on the Integrations page.

VersionDiscontinued.description: The API version this request is answered under has been discontinued. Send a supported version in `Lingara-Version`, or re-pin the client.

Gone.description: `api_version_discontinued`: this request's API version has been discontinued. `cursor_expired`: the cursor is older than 30 days; start again without one.

Unavailable.description: The service is temporarily unavailable; retry after the number of seconds in `Retry-After`. During maintenance the body is plain text rather than the error envelope.

ledger.description: This client's calls and units since midnight UTC on the first of the month. Present only for a metered client, whose calls spend no allowance. It can trail your latest call by up to five seconds.

code.description: Why the request was refused, as a stable code to branch on: for example `insufficient_scope` (`403`), `rate_limited` (`429`), `api_allowance_exhausted` (`429`) and, for a metered client, `spend_cap_reached` (`402`) and `metered_billing_inactive` (`402`).

plan_status.description: The plan's status when the event was accepted. Only `generating` promises that `lesson_plan.ready` or `lesson_plan.failed` will follow. Any other value is a plan served from the library, which you can read now with `GET /v1/lesson-plans/{id}`.

player_ref.description: Your own reference for the player: 1 to 128 bytes of UTF-8, with no control characters. Lingara stores only a hash of it.

embed_version.description: The embed version your game build runs, as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Send it to be told when an update is available. Only a caller that sends it is warned about, or refused on, a yanked version.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires, counted from this answer. Use it when the device's clock cannot be trusted.

update_available.description: Present only when the request named an `embed_version` that is behind the serving version, deprecated, or withdrawn.

latest.description: The version now serving, or null when no published version serves.

deprecated.description: Whether the developer deprecated the version you declared.

message.description: The developer's deprecation message, verbatim and never translated, or null.

subject.description: The account's `lgr_sub_`: what this player's events carry from now on.

previous_subject.description: The guest's `lgr_sub_`: what the player's earlier events keep. Route both to the same `player_ref`.

linked_at.description: When the link was made. On an `existing` answer, the first call's time.

scopes.description: The most a token for this player can now hold: what the account granted, of the scopes a player's token can carry.

carried.description: Rows this call moved to the account, per table. Only tables with a count appear.

kept.description: Rows this call left with the guest, per table: a plan still being written, or a row the account already had. Call again once `lesson_plans` here has a plan that has finished.

LinkStatus.description: `linked`: this call made the link. `existing`: it was already live for this account, and the counts are only what this call moved.

pedagogy.description: `subtle` (the default) keeps the character's `target_lang` at or below the learner's `level`. `none` lets the character speak at its own level, as a native speaker when it has no `languages`, and ignores `level`.

history.description: The conversation so far, oldest first, at most 12 lines. You keep the window: Lingara stores nothing between turns. Send each NPC reply back cut to its first 500 characters.

checkpoint.description: Where the story stands: a goal the character steers toward, and the facts it may reveal. Needs `enable_npc_dialogue_graphs`.

edges.description: The ways out of this checkpoint whose game conditions already hold, each with a plain-language condition. After the reply, at most one is chosen and sent as a `transition` event before `done`. Edges your game decides on its own are never sent.

languages.description: The languages this character knows, each with how well it speaks and how well it understands, on the same 1–9 scale as `level`. Use the same codes as `source_lang` and `target_lang`. A language not listed is one the character neither speaks nor understands. The character answers in `target_lang` if it is listed, else in `source_lang` if that is, else in its strongest language, which must then be one Lingara offers as a target language. Leave the list out and the character speaks `target_lang`.

DialogueTransition.description: The edge the conversation just crossed. Move your story to `to`. If no edge was crossed, no `transition` is sent; a `transition_unavailable` notice means the check could not run this turn.

CanvasDefinition.description: A canvas: its nodes and the edges between them. `fields` is the editor's own state; the dry-run, not this schema, judges content.

DialogueRule.description: Which check a `dialogue_invalid` or `dialogue_graph_invalid` refusal failed, beside its `path`.

CanvasVerdictKind.description: No `would_replace`: a changed webhook endpoint becomes a new version, so it is `would_update`.
